headline: Profit rebounds on easy comps while core earnings hold flat
summary_short: Aflac's Q1 2026 net earnings jumped to $1,019M ($1.98 diluted EPS) from just $29M a year ago as last year's large net investment losses did not recur, while total revenue rose 27.9% y/y to $4,346M; adjusted earnings, which strip out investment gains/losses, were roughly flat at $901M vs $906M a year ago.
summary_long: GAAP net earnings surged to $1.0 billion ($1.98/diluted share) from $29 million a year earlier, driven almost entirely by the absence of 2025's large net investment losses (Q1 2025 included $963M of investment losses vs a $49M gain this quarter); adjusted earnings, which exclude investment gains/losses, were roughly flat at $901M (-0.6% y/y) as Aflac Japan's pretax adjusted earnings rose 8.3% (yen basis) on favorable benefits while Aflac U.S. pretax adjusted earnings grew 1.4%. The yen averaged 2.8% weaker y/y, trimming adjusted EPS by $0.02. Shareholders' equity rose to $30.0 billion; the company returned $1.3 billion to shareholders ($1.0B buyback, $315M dividends) and raised its Q2 dividend 5.2% to $0.61/share. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Q1 2025 included $963M of net investment losses (mainly derivative and CECL-driven) versus a $49M net investment gain this quarter, per the release's own reconciliation; this swing accounts for nearly all of the y/y net-earnings jump.
Total revenues rose y/y primarily on the swing from net investment losses to gains embedded in GAAP revenue; adjusted (ex-investment-gains) revenue actually declined, per the segment tables.

Aflac Japan pretax adjusted earnings rose 8.3% (yen basis) on favorable benefits experience, while Aflac U.S. pretax adjusted earnings grew 1.4% on improved sales and persistency, per the release's segment discussion.
A lower weighted-average diluted share count (514.8M vs 546.9M y/y), reflecting continued buybacks, added to the per-share gain beyond the rise in total net earnings.
Adjusted earnings per diluted share, which exclude investment gains/losses, rose only 5.4% to $1.75 as a 2.8% weaker yen trimmed adjusted EPS by $0.02; the release issued no new forward guidance.
